editorial:
Imagine losing your phone and thinking you are lucky to get it back, only to realize the person who found it is actually a monster. You will feel the tension immediately as you watch the main character, a hardworking woman, slowly realize that a stranger has hacked into her entire life. The vibe is super creepy because it plays on a fear we all have: our phones know everything about us. It is not just a crime story; it is a scary look at how easy it is for someone to track your every move, read your texts, and ruin your reputation without you even knowing they are there.

The acting is top-notch, especially the villain who is truly terrifying in how calm he stays while doing horrible things. The pacing is quick, so you will not get bored, though some of the plot twists feel a bit predictable if you watch a lot of thrillers. Still, the suspense keeps you glued to the screen. If you want the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the detail, or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a movie night. It is a great pick for anyone who likes stories about digital stalking.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a brutal showdown between the main character and the hacker. After a terrifying game of cat and mouse, the woman manages to fight back and survive the attacker's final attempt to kill her. The police arrive just in time to stop him. It wraps up by showing how the villain used a simple app to control her life, leaving you with a scary reminder to change your passwords and be careful with your devices.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves suspenseful stories about hackers and crime.
